promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Skip the make-up miles. Heat, short sleep and a work deadline pushed your easy heart rate up 13 bpm, so next week is a steady 31 mi built around a calm 12 mi long run.

flags.title: Short of the plan
flags.detail: Wednesday stopped after 2 of 3 reps, Thursday was missed and Sunday ended at 11 of 13 mi. The heat and short sleep explain it, and none of it gets made up.

flags.title: Easy heart rate
flags.detail: It averaged 151 bpm on easy runs, 13 bpm above your normal. Keep easy runs under 145 bpm, even if the pace feels embarrassingly slow.

flags.detail: You averaged 5.5 hours. If you sleep under 6 hours the night before Thursday, skip that run. The sleep will help you more than 4 easy miles.

flags.title: Heat
flags.detail: Run before sunrise or on a treadmill if you can. Carry water on anything over an hour, and judge every run by heart rate, not pace.

flags.detail: You did 0 of 2 sessions. The hip and glute routine helped settle your knee in August, so do 15 minutes after the Tuesday and Thursday runs.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No, don't make up the miles. You've lost the missed Thursday and the 2 mi cut from Sunday, and that's fine. Adding them back would pile more work onto a body that's already short on sleep and dealing with heat.

Your fitness for Nov 1 will come from stringing together steady weeks over the next two months, not from any single run. Next week is about 31 mi with a 12 mi long run. Keep it that way even if you feel fresh by the weekend.

new.analysis:
**You ran 27 of the 36 planned miles, and every run was harder than planned.**

| Day | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue | 6 mi easy | 6 mi, avg HR 153 |
| Wed | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 6 mi, 2 reps at 8:18/mi |
| Thu | 5 mi easy | missed |
| Sat | 4 mi easy | 4 mi, avg HR 149 |
| Sun | 13 mi, HR under 150 | 11 mi, avg HR 156 |
| Total | 36 mi | 27 mi |

**Everything happening outside running caught up with you at once.** Your body counts heat, a broken AC, 5.5 hours of sleep and a work deadline as stress, just like training. That's why your easy heart rate rose 13 bpm while your pace slowed by almost 30 seconds per mile.

**The week was much harder than its mileage suggests.** Only about 11 percent of your running time was in the easy zones, against a target of 80. Nearly every easy mile was in zone 3, which explains feeling drained better than the missed miles do.

**One hot week doesn't change the goal.** Under 3:45 means about 8:35/mi. Your threshold reps at about 8:00/mi in early August fit that well. Your fitness is still there, just hidden under the heat and fatigue.

**Next week is a little lighter and much easier than last week.** It's about 31 mi against last week's 36 planned, with easy runs set by heart rate instead of pace. The one session is at marathon effort instead of threshold, which costs less and is still specific to the race. Thursday can drop out on short sleep, which still leaves you about 27 mi.

**The long run needs protecting more than the weekly total does.** Your longest run is still 12 mi, and it has to build toward about 3 hours by early October. There's room for that, but only if the next few long runs go well. That's why Sunday is about finishing in control, not covering extra distance.

**Your easy heart rate tells us when to push again.** Once the AC is fixed and you're back near 7 hours of sleep, it should drop to the high 130s. When it does, threshold work comes back and the long run steps up. If it stays high even with good sleep, we hold back longer.

settingsProposalBullets: Injury history: the outside of your right knee hurt on the Aug 16 long run and settled within a week of lighter running and hip and glute work.
A 15-minute hip and glute routine twice a week is a standing part of your training.
In cool weather your easy runs sit at about 138 to 140 bpm at around 9:50 to 10:00/mi. This is your baseline for spotting fatigue and heat stress.

safetyCallouts.title: Know the heat warning signs.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel dizzy, sick, confused or get chills while running in the heat, stop, get somewhere cool and drink. Get medical help if it doesn't settle quickly.

safetyCallouts.title: See a doctor if the tiredness lingers.
safetyCallouts.body: If you still feel tired all the time once the AC is fixed and your sleep is back to normal, get checked rather than training through it.
